exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Inverse of a Reciprocal Function

question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

\[ y = \dfrac{3}{4x+1} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x = \dfrac{3}{4y+1}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= \dfrac{3}{4y+1} \\[5pt] x(4y+1) &= 3 \\[5pt] 4xy + x &= 3 \\[5pt] 4xy &= 3 - x\\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{3- x}{4x} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{3-x}{4x}. \]

question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

\[ y = \dfrac{6}{5x+3} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x = \dfrac{6}{5y+3}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= \dfrac{6}{5y+3} \\[5pt] x(5y+3) &= 6 \\[5pt] 5xy + 3x &= 6 \\[5pt] 5xy &= 6 - 3x \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{6- 3x}{5x} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{6-3x}{5x}. \]

example.title: Finding the Inverse of a Reciprocal Function

question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

\[ y = \dfrac{8}{4-x} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x = \dfrac{8}{4-y}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= \dfrac{8}{4-y} \\[5pt] x(4-y) &= 8 \\[5pt] 4x - xy &= 8 \\[5pt] -xy &= 8- 4x \\[5pt] xy &= 4x-8 \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{4x-8}{x} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{4x-8}{x}. \]

example.title: Finding the Inverse of a Reciprocal Function

question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

\[ y = \dfrac{1}{(2x+1)^2} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x = \dfrac{1}{(2y+1)^2}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= \dfrac{1}{(2y+1)^2} \\[5pt] (2y+1)^2 &= \dfrac{1}{x} \\[5pt] \sqrt{(2y+1)^2} &= \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{x}} \\[5pt] |2y +1| &= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}} \\[5pt] 2y + 1 &= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}} \\[5pt] 2y & = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}} - 1 \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} - \dfrac{1}{2} \end{align}

Note that we used the fact that for $y > -\dfrac{1}{2},$ we have \[ |2y+1| = 2y+1. \]

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}} -\dfrac{1}{2} . \]

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Inverse of a Simple Rational Function

question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

\[ y = \dfrac{5 - 2x}{x+1} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x = \dfrac{5- 2y}{y+1}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= \dfrac{5 - 2y}{y+1} \\[5pt] x(y+1) &= 5 - 2y \\[5pt] xy + x &= 5 - 2y \\[5pt] xy + 2y &= 5 - x \\[5pt] y(x+2) &= 5 - x \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{5-x}{x+2} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{5-x}{x+2}. \]

example.title: Finding the Inverse of a Simple Rational Function

question.text: Find the inverse of the function $f(x) = \dfrac{1 - x}{2x + 3}.$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

\[ y = \dfrac{1 - x}{2x+3} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x = \dfrac{1 - y}{2y + 3}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= \dfrac{1 -y}{2y+3} \\[5pt] x(2y+3) &= 1 - y \\[5pt] 2xy + 3x &= 1 - y \\[5pt] 2xy + y &= 1 - 3x \\[5pt] y(2x+1) &= 1 - 3x \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{1 - 3x}{2x+1} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{1 - 3x}{2x+1}}. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Determining an Unknown Value Given the Inverse of a Rational Function

question.text: The function $f(x),$ defined as \[ f(x) = \dfrac{4}{(x+k)^2}, \qquad x \gt -k \] has an inverse function given by \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{x}}- 5, \qquad x \gt 0. \] What is the value of $k?$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

\[ y = \dfrac{4}{(x+k)^2} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x =\dfrac{4}{(y+k)^2}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= \dfrac{4}{(y+k)^2} \\[5pt] (y + k)^2 &= \dfrac{4}{x} \\[5pt] \sqrt{(y + k)^2} &= \sqrt{\dfrac{4}{x}} \\[5pt] |y +k| &= \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{x}} \\[5pt] y + k &= \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{x}} \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{x}} - k \end{align}

Note that we used the fact that for $y \gt -k,$ we have \[ |y+k| = y+k. \]

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{x}} - k . \]

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=5.$

example.title: Determining an Unknown Value Given the Inverse of a Rational Function

question.text: The function $f(x) = \dfrac{3}{4 + kx}$ has an inverse function given by $f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{3-4x}{2x}.$ What is the value of $k?$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

\[ y = \dfrac{3}{4 + kx} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x = \dfrac{3}{4 +ky}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= \dfrac{3}{4 + ky} \\[5pt] x(4 + ky) &= 3 \\[5pt] 4x + kxy &= 3\\[5pt] kxy &=3 - 4x\\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{3 -4x}{kx} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{3 -4x}{kx}. \]

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=2.$

question.text: The function $f(x) = \dfrac{3}{kx-2}$ has an inverse function given by $f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{3+2x}{5x}.$ What is the value of $k?$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

\[ y = \dfrac{3}{kx-2} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x = \dfrac{3}{ky-2}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= \dfrac{3}{ky-2} \\[5pt] x(ky-2) &= 3 \\[5pt] kxy - 2x &= 3 \\[5pt] kxy &= 3 + 2x\\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{3+2x}{kx} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{3 + 2x}{kx}. \]

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=5.$

question.text: The function $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{7x + k}$ has an inverse function given by $f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{1 +3x}{7x}.$ What is the value of $k?$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

\[ y = \dfrac{1}{7x + k} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x = \dfrac{1}{7y + k}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= \dfrac{1}{7y + k} \\[5pt] x(7y + k) &= 1 \\[5pt] 7xy + kx &= 1 \\[5pt] 7xy &= 1 -kx \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{1- kx}{7x} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{1 -kx}{7x}. \]

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=-3.$
